defects.canonical: release() returns the connection to the idle list without calling conn.rollback() (or commit), so an open/uncommitted transaction from the previous holder rides along to the next acquirer, who may unknowingly commit or be blocked by held locks.
defects.why_subtle: release looks complete and defensive (closed check, discard), and the missing rollback is an absence rather than a wrong line a skimmer can point at.

defects.canonical: Per-session state (search_path set via set_active_tenant, plus any SET session vars or temp tables) is never reset on release, so the next tenant that acquires the same physical connection inherits the prior tenant's search_path and reads/writes the wrong schema (cross-tenant state bleed).
defects.why_subtle: The tenant switch happens in a separate method, so reviewing release() in isolation gives no hint that recycled connections carry session state across tenants.

defects.canonical: set_active_tenant builds the SET search_path statement via string interpolation of the caller-supplied tenant value, a textbook SQL injection.
defects.why_subtle: Intentional calibration anchor: classic %-format string concatenation of an untrusted value into SQL, flagged on sight.
